h1: The 4 Best Walk-Behind Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four wheeled walk-behind leaf blowers compared on listed airflow, engine size and price for large lawns, lots and driveways.
summary: The Champion 212cc is the best walk-behind blower here, with a stated 1200 CFM and engine size. The Yardmax lists the same airflow for less money, making it the value pick. The SuperHandy and Landworks trail because their listings leave out airflow, so confirm those numbers before buying.
intro: Think of a walk-behind blower as a snow plow for leaves. You push it across open ground and it clears a wide swath with each pass, which is why the format suits big lawns and long driveways and feels clumsy anywhere tight. Buyers who pick one for a townhouse yard usually end up storing a very large machine they rarely use.

We ranked four walk-behind models using what each listing states about airflow, engine and fuel, plus the price range. Backpack blowers are a separate tool and stay out. Two of these four omit key figures, so the ranking rewards products that publish clear specs and flags the gaps.

products.name: Champion Power Equipment 212cc 1200 CFM Walk-Behind Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The best-specified walk-behind here, with 212cc and 1200 CFM.
products.description:
The Champion Power Equipment blower is a gas walk-behind with a 212cc engine and a listed 1200 CFM of airflow. It is the only model in the ranking priced at $500 and above, and its listing states both headline numbers plainly.

It leads for exactly that reason. Engine size and airflow let you judge the machine before you buy, which cannot be said for the two models near the bottom. Against the Yardmax, which lists the same 1200 CFM, the extra money buys a confirmed engine size and a better-known brand name.

Buy it for a large lot, a long driveway or heavy autumn leaf fall. The caveat is cost and bulk: it is the most expensive blower here, and it needs real garage space. Owners of small yards should look elsewhere.
products.idealFor: Large lots, driveways and heavy leaf fall.
products.skipIf: You have a small yard or tight budget.

products.name: Yardmax Gas Walk-Behind Blower
products.verdict: The same 1200 CFM as the Champion, in a lower price range.
products.description:
The Yardmax is a gas walk-behind blower that lists 1200 CFM and falls in the $200 to $500 range. That is the same airflow as the Champion above it, delivered for a lower price.

It ranks second because the savings come with a gap. Our data shows no engine size for it, so you cannot compare power the way you can with the 212cc Champion. The brand is also less familiar, which makes support harder to judge. If the missing detail does not bother you, this is the smarter spend.

Buy it if you have an open lot and want strong airflow without the top-tier price. Before ordering, confirm the engine size on the current listing, because that is the one number you cannot verify here.
products.idealFor: Large lots on a smaller budget.
products.skipIf: You want the engine size confirmed.

products.name: SuperHandy Walk Behind Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A walk-behind from SuperHandy, sold under two listings, one noting gas.
products.description:
The SuperHandy walk-behind blower is priced in the $200 to $500 range. A second listing under the same name notes gas power, so two product pages exist for what may be one machine, and they do not agree on detail.

It is third because the missing airflow figure makes it impossible to rank against the 1200 CFM picks. A mid-priced wheeled blower may well be capable, yet nothing in the data proves it, and double listings add confusion about which version arrives at your door.

Buy it if you already prefer the SuperHandy name and plan to verify airflow, engine and fuel type on the page first. Skip it if you want a decision based on numbers, because the Yardmax gives you those for similar money.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer the SuperHandy brand.

products.name: Landworks Leaf Blower Wheeled Walk Behind Jet Sweep Manual-Propelled
products.verdict: A wheeled, manually pushed gas jet sweeper.
products.description:
The Landworks is a wheeled gas jet sweeper that you push by hand, listed in the $200 to $500 range. Pushing rather than self-propelling keeps it simpler, though slopes will test your legs.

It ranks fourth because no airflow figure appears in our data, and the manual drive adds a physical cost over the higher-ranked models. Jet sweepers are made for moving debris across open ground, which suits some jobs, but without a CFM figure we cannot tell whether it matches the others.

Buy it for flat, open areas such as a parking pad or a wide drive, where pushing a blower beats carrying one. Check airflow before ordering. If you have a hill, the extra effort will quickly become a reason to pick another machine.
products.idealFor: Open areas where pushing beats carrying.

whatMatters.detail: Airflow in CFM tells you how much air the machine pushes per minute, which indicates how quickly a wide row of leaves will clear. At the top end, walk-behind models here list 1200 CFM. Scan the title or bullets for it, and be wary of a listing that omits it, as two of these four do.

Engine size in cubic centimeters hints at how much power the blower has. The Champion lists 212cc, a common size for outdoor power equipment. It matters because a larger engine usually sustains airflow on wet or heavy debris. Check the cc figure in the title or spec table, and note any listing that leaves it out.

A manually pushed blower is lighter and mechanically simpler, but you supply the effort on slopes and long runs. A self-propelled one removes that strain at a higher price. The Landworks is described as manually propelled. Read how the listing describes drive, and picture the longest uphill stretch you would cover.

Walk-behind blowers are large and take real floor space in a garage or shed. A wheeled frame helps with moving it, but not with storage. This matters if your space is tight. Look for dimensions on the listing, measure your storage spot, and allow room to get around the machine.

Price ranges here start at $200 to $500 and rise above $500 for the Champion. Higher cost usually buys clearer specs and a stronger brand, not always more airflow, since the Yardmax matches the Champion's 1200 CFM. Compare the CFM and engine data before paying extra, and treat a missing spec as a reason for caution.

faq.q: Is a walk-behind blower right for a small yard?
faq.a: Usually not. Walk-behind blowers like the Champion 212cc are sized for open ground, and the frame is awkward in tight spaces. On a small lot a handheld is easier to maneuver, store and afford.

Skipping airflow. Two of these four, the SuperHandy and the Landworks, do not state CFM in our data, which makes comparison guesswork. Prefer a model like the Champion or Yardmax that lists 1200 CFM on the page.

faq.q: Is the Champion worth it over the Yardmax?
faq.a: Both list 1200 CFM. The Champion adds a stated 212cc engine and a stronger brand, but it costs far more than the Yardmax. Pay the premium only if a confirmed engine matters to you.

The Yardmax and Landworks are listed as gas. The SuperHandy has a second listing that notes gas power, and the Champion's 212cc engine points to gas too. Confirm fuel type on the exact page before ordering.

Plan for garage or shed space, because a walk-behind unit like the Champion is bulky compared with a handheld. Measure the floor area and door width first. A wheeled frame makes moving it simple, but not smaller.

Backpack blowers are a different category from walk-behind models. They are carried on the shoulders rather than pushed, so they suit different yards and jobs. Comparing the two types in one ranking would not be fair to either.

finalTake: Choose the Champion if you want a walk-behind blower whose spec sheet leaves nothing to guess. Take the Yardmax when the same 1200 CFM at a lower price matters more than a stated engine size. Treat the SuperHandy and Landworks as options only after the missing airflow figures are confirmed on the listing.
